$comment: Documentation versions. One entry per documentation line the site serves.
Exactly one entry has "default": true, and it is the latest stable release: a reader who follows a bare /docs
link, or arrives from a search engine, lands on documentation for a package they can actually install.
content/docs           the working documentation, tracking the source tree in this repository. It describes the
version under development and is the only tree the repository documentation gates check.
content/versions/<id>  a frozen snapshot of a released line. Snapshots are never edited in place, and the
linters leave them alone because their snippets reference source that has since moved.
1. Copy content/docs to content/versions/<previous id> if that line has no snapshot yet.
2. Move "default": true to the entry for the newly released line.
3. Set that entry's "status" to "stable" and update "release" and "ref".
"ref" is the git ref a version's Markdown sources live on, used for fallback links into the repository.
A line that is still on its own release branch names that branch; it becomes "main" when the line merges.
This file is JSON rather than TypeScript because the build gates in site/scripts read it from plain Node.
